content: embedded-graphics-framebuf 0.5.0 only ships FrameBufferBackend impls for fixed-size arrays ([C;N]/&mut [C;N]), not Vec<C> (and can't be added downstream due to orphan rules - both the trait and Vec are foreign). Solution: a local newtype (HeapBuffer(Vec<Rgb565>)) implementing FrameBufferBackend, which keeps FrameBuffer565's resolution a runtime parameter instead of a compile-time const generic. Also: DrawTargetExt::clipped(&area) does NOT translate coordinates into area-relative space, it only clips - widgets must still draw in absolute framebuffer coordinates offset by area.top_left.

Bash tool cwd persists across calls, so a cd into a worktree silently retargets every later git command - a merge then reports Already up to date because it ran on the branch being merged. Use absolute paths or cd back explicitly.

core has no core::time::Instant; introduced platform::Instant (a u64-microseconds newtype with saturating_duration_since + Add<Duration>) that every Clock impl converts to at the trait boundary. HostClock now records a std::time::Instant epoch at construction and reports elapsed micros since it. Also moved std::thread::sleep out of run() entirely into Clock::sleep(&self, Duration) -- run.rs:93 rationale block flipped from 'thread::sleep works on every target' to 'no_std has no std::thread, so the platform decides what blocking means'. run.rs:411's std::error::Error mention was pure doc-comment wording (StubFlushError only ever derived Debug) -- reworded, no code changed.

cc::Build (per-file compile + incremental ar) avoids the previous attempt's 'argument list too long' - that came from a single giant gcc invocation with hundreds of source files on the command line, not from any real toolchain limit. Any future C cross-compile probe should default to cc::Build or an explicit response-file Makefile, never a hand-rolled shell one-liner.

panic-halt's bare loop{} silently converts any panic into what looks like a total, USB-independent hang. The real bug (CONTROL_BUF too small - see parallel investigation's comment) panicked inside usb_task's poll on core0's cooperative executor, not inside the USBCTRL_IRQ ISR; because panic-halt never unwinds, Executor::run() never regained control to poll ANY other task, which starved watchdog_feed_task and the old async-Timer safety_net_task right along with USB. That is why a 180s 'independent' safety net never fired even after 15+ minutes - it was never USB-independent in the first place, since it shared an executor with the thing that panicked. Fixed both: grew CONTROL_BUF 64B->256B (root cause - config.product needs 78 bytes as UTF-16LE, only 64 were available), and replaced panic_halt with a #[panic_handler] that calls reset_to_usb_boot() directly so any FUTURE panic self-recovers in ~0s instead of relying on the 8s hardware watchdog or wedging forever. General lesson for this board: a bare halt-loop panic handler is actively hostile to unattended iteration on a target with no RTT/probe - it makes every panic indistinguishable from a genuine deadlock, which is the expensive kind of bug to diagnose blind.

BTstack's btstack_run_loop_embedded.c is gated on HAVE_EMBEDDED_TICK vs HAVE_EMBEDDED_TIME_MS at compile time (mutually exclusive, #error if both defined). btstack_config.h in this spike already set HAVE_EMBEDDED_TIME_MS, so hal_tick_init/hal_tick_set_handler/hal_tick_get_tick_period_in_ms were NEVER CALLED even before this bead - confirmed by grep, all three call sites in btstack_run_loop_embedded.c are inside '#ifdef HAVE_EMBEDDED_TICK' blocks that were compiled out. Deleted them rather than leaving dead stubs, per the bead's ask. Also: nestable hal_cpu_disable_irqs/enable_irqs needs a depth counter, not a save/restore of PRIMASK's prior state - BTstack's own call sites (run loop + hci.c/l2cap.c critical sections) always pair disable/enable 1:1 with no interleaving from other code, so a simple 0<->N counter (only the 0->1 transition masks, only the 1->0 transition unmasks) is sufficient and correct; verified by reading every call site, not by fuzzing actual nesting on hardware. Also: hal_cpu_enable_irqs_and_sleep must NOT do a real WFI unless the core actually has an unmasked periodic interrupt source configured on its own NVIC - core1 here has none, so WFI would sleep forever and silently kill the run loop's idle path. This would have been a nasty one to debug blind (looks identical to 'BTstack is stuck', not obviously a sleep-forever bug) if not caught by reading hal_cpu_enable_irqs_and_sleep's call site in btstack_run_loop_embedded_execute_once before implementing it.

embassy-usb's class.write_packet().await BLOCKS (backpressure) when nothing is draining the CDC bulk endpoint - it does not error on host disconnect. A debug console loop that reads-then-writes-then-loops (like console_task here) will therefore hold a stale snapshot across any disconnect and deliver it late, then resume live, on reconnect. Two backlogged lines draining back-to-back at reconnect (timestamped within ~100ms of each other) is indistinguishable, if you only look at PRINTED deltas, from either a burst or a stall in the thing being measured. Any future debug telemetry over a blocking CDC/serial channel needs to be judged skeptically against this artifact before blaming the subsystem it's reporting on - prefer non-blocking/dropping writes (or a channel that can't back up) for anything used to diagnose timing bugs.

RP2350's pico-sdk hardware_gpio/gpio.c uses a NEW-to-RP2350 'GPIO coprocessor' fast path (gpioc_bit_oe_put etc, a CP0 custom instruction) not present on RP2040. A Rust-owned binary that bypasses pico-sdk's own crt0/runtime_init (as this one deliberately does, per the ADR) never enables CP0 access, so the FIRST call to gpio_set_dir/gpio_set_pulls (cyw43_init's WL_REG_ON pin config) takes a UsageFault/NOCP (CFSR 0x80000). Fix: OR M33 CPACR (0xE000ED88, standard ARMv8-M address) with 0x3 (CP0 full access) once per core, before any pico-sdk GPIO call - this replicates pico-sdk's own runtime_init_per_core_enable_coprocessors() (one register write), not its whole init-table walk. Confirmed via a HardFault handler dumping PC/LR/CFSR over CDC: PC landed exactly inside gpioc_bit_oe_put. This will bite pico-link-xkp.2 (TinyUSB dcd) too if TinyUSB's RP2350 dcd also uses any GPIO/hardware coprocessor fast path - worth checking there before re-deriving this.

cyw43-driver's LICENSE.RP (not its default LICENSE, which is non-commercial-only) is the applicable one here - it grants unrestricted commercial use as long as the software runs 'solely with... RP2040 or any other semiconductor device produced by [Raspberry Pi Ltd]'. RP2350 qualifies (same Licensor). So linking cyw43-driver is fine for Pico Link commercially, AS LONG AS this firmware only ever targets Raspberry Pi silicon - flag this if the product roadmap ever considers a non-RP MCU.

bd show exits 0 for a nonexistent bead ID and only prints an error line, so exit status cannot validate an ID. Use bd show ID --json and check that the result parses as an array whose first element has the expected id - the miss returns an object with an error key instead.

nm check (day-1, per bead) on the ui-ffi staticlib for thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf: memcpy/memset/memmove/memcmp and every __aeabi_* symbol from compiler_builtins are WEAK (W), not strong (T) -- they yield to newlib's strong definitions at final link with zero collision risk, no --allow-multiple-definition and no objcopy --localize-symbol needed. The only undefined (U) symbols found were _critical_section_1_0_acquire/_release (from embedded-alloc's LlffHeap, which needs a critical_section::Impl registered) -- addressing with a hand-rolled cpsid/cpsie primask impl in ui-ffi, not cortex-m-rt (forbidden by the bead).

the bead's ui-ffi target triple as literally written (thumbv8m.main-none-eabihf) fails final link against pico-sdk's build of this board with 'uses VFP register arguments, pico_link.elf does not' (every ui-ffi object file). pico-sdk builds this board's C code softfp (see its thumb/v8-m.main+fp/softfp object path -- hardware FPU instructions allowed, but integer registers for the calling convention), while Rust's ...eabihf target uses hardfloat (VFP register) argument passing -- an ABI mismatch, not a bug in the FFI surface itself. Fixed by switching ui-ffi's cross-compile target to thumbv8m.main-none-eabi (soft-float, no hf suffix) in firmware/CMakeLists.txt -- its calling convention (integer registers for float args) matches pico-sdk's softfp exactly, and it links clean. Also added 'rustup target add' as a build-command prefix since this target isn't installed by default.

heap fix (192KB) confirmed working on hardware. Flashed twice; both times the device settled into a stable, monotonically-incrementing heartbeat loop (11-19, then after a fresh reflash 5-15) with zero resets/crashes -- strong evidence the full pl_ui_create -> pl_ui_render -> pl_ui_input -> pl_ui_tick -> pl_ui_render sequence in main.c executes successfully on real hardware without faulting (a HardFault or alloc-error trap before the heartbeat loop would prevent it from ever being reached, let alone incrementing cleanly across two separate boots). Did not manage to capture the actual boot-banner/pl_ui_render sample-pixel diagnostic text over CDC in either attempt -- by the time the tty_fallback reader connects and DTR raises, TinyUSB's console ring buffer has already moved past those early lines (only ~1.5-5s of runtime, mostly consumed by the boot sleep_ms(1500)). This is a host-side capture-timing race, not a firmware issue; the absence of any crash/reset is itself sufficient evidence the FFI path worked. Continuing to stage 4 (ST7789 driver port) next.

full hardware pipeline (backlight -> RGB solid fills -> pl_ui_create -> input init -> render+blit loop) flashed and ran successfully, captured over CDC: 'panel: solid BLUE fill' / 'pl_ui_create OK' / 'pl_link_input_init OK' / 'frame 1: render=26624us blit=1008027us total=1034694us'. The ~1.008s blit is NOT a bug -- it is the expected DMA transfer time at the deliberately-conservative 1MHz SPI clock: 240*240*16 bits = 921,600 bits / 1e6 Hz = 0.9216s, matching the measurement almost exactly. This is why the bead says keep the clock low until CS framing is confirmed and NOT to bump it prematurely -- I have NOT bumped the clock, since confirming panel framing/colors requires a human (or webcam) looking at the actual panel, which I could not do in this environment (no camera capture CLI tool found on this Mac in this session). CDC output only ever captured a few lines per read due to a host-side timing race (tty_fallback connects a couple seconds after boot, missing the earliest banner/fill lines) -- not a firmware issue; every capture that did land showed clean, expected progression with zero crashes/resets across 3 separate flashes. HANDOFF TO ANDREAS: please visually confirm on the physical panel (or webcam) that the R/G/B fill sequence at boot shows correct, non-inverted colors in the right order, and that the joystick/buttons move the placeholder list's selection once the render loop starts. If colors are wrong, the bug is isolated to firmware/src/st7789.c (zero Rust involved in the fill sequence). Once framing is confirmed, ST7789_INIT_BAUDRATE_HZ in st7789.h can be raised (e.g. to 40-62MHz) to bring frame time down from ~1s to the tens-of-ms range.

the M1b panel renders correct GEOMETRY but wrong COLOUR. Orchestrator compared a settled webcam frame against the emulator headless PNG of the same root screen: empty background area is (8,16,32) near-black navy in the emulator and photographs as (167,248,245) on the panel - the brightest region in frame. Near-black cannot photograph as the brightest thing at any exposure, so inversion is established. Layout, text, rows and footer are pixel-correct, so the FFI seam, core rendering and the DMA blit are all proven RIGHT; the fault is confined to colour mapping in firmware/src/st7789.c. Channel order is NOT established - camera auto white balance swung warm between captures, so R-vs-B readings are untrustworthy while luminance is. The decisive test is the R/G/B solid-fill sequence with zero Rust in it, classified by chroma: red photographing as cyan means inversion, red as blue means channel order.

.claude/frontend-reviews-requirement.md was not the only dead frontend-review boilerplate - discovery.md also had a step-5 block appending supervisor names to .claude/frontend-supervisors.txt for a 'frontend reviews hook' that does not exist in .claude/hooks/, plus RAMS/WIG entries in its completion report and quality checklist. Deleting only the named file would have left dangling instructions. Removed all of it. .claude/ui-constraints.md (Tailwind/React/Base UI rules) is the same class of dead template boilerplate but was left in place: it is out of this bead's scope and is only injected for react/vue/svelte supervisors that will never be created here.

core/src/app.rs root screen is now a live devices list (LinkState/DeviceEntry/Command types), driven via App::set_link_state/add_device/clear_devices/poll_command, all committed and host-tested green. Next: extend ui-ffi with pl_ui_set_link_state/pl_ui_add_device/pl_ui_clear_devices/pl_ui_poll_command, then the C-side BTstack wiring.

the PATH arm-none-eabi-gcc (Homebrew formula, /opt/homebrew/bin) is missing newlib specs (nosys.specs etc) -- 'cannot read spec file nosys.specs'. The real toolchain is the gcc-arm-embedded CASK at /Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin -- configure CMake with -DPICO_TOOLCHAIN_PATH=/Applications/ArmGNUToolchain/15.2.rel1/arm-none-eabi/bin. Worth adding to CLAUDE.md's firmware-build notes so it isn't rediscovered.

with the M2 build flashed, the board DOES enumerate USB CDC (picotool sees a USB serial connection, 0x2e8a:0x0009) yet cdc_reader.py claims the interface cleanly and reads ZERO bytes in 8 seconds, and the panel photographs at (22,20,21) - genuinely dark. Do NOT infer from enumeration that main() ran: pico-sdk stdio_usb services TinyUSB from a timer/IRQ context and with PICO_STDIO_USB_ENABLE_RESET_VIA_VENDOR_INTERFACE=1 that keeps running while main() is hung, so USB being up is fully consistent with a hang in the first lines of main(). What it does rule out is the measurement-artifact hypothesis: the capture path works and there is genuinely nothing being printed. The untested variables are not the BT code, which was already compiled out with the same symptom, but the two build-config changes that stayed in the binary either way - PICO_STACK_SIZE=0xC000 and the mere linking of pico_btstack_classic, pico_btstack_cyw43 and pico_cyw43_arch_threadsafe_background.

root cause of the CDC silence (coordinator identified, I verified): pico-sdk's stdio_usb gates ALL console output on DTR by default (stdio_usb_connected() -> tud_cdc_connected()), and tools/usb-console/cdc_reader.py cannot assert DTR on macOS (EACCES on the CDC-Communication interface, bead pico-link-4mc) -- so a healthy board was indistinguishable from a hung one, always zero bytes. Fix: PICO_STDIO_USB_CONNECTION_WITHOUT_DTR=1 in target_compile_definitions (firmware/CMakeLists.txt, committed 68d1285). VERIFIED on the M1b baseline (rebuilt in /tmp/pl-baseline-check with the flag added, not committed there -- throwaway checkout): cdc_reader.py now captures the real boot banner and FILL_HOLD/FILL_START markers. Console is now a trustworthy signal for the M2 bisection.

RAM layout check (arm-none-eabi-size + nm) on the full M2 build (BT linked, PICO_STACK_SIZE=0xC000): .bss ends at 0x2003589c, stack region is 0x20076000-0x20082000 -- about 263KB of headroom between them, no collision with the 192KB Rust heap arena or BTstack's static buffers. Stack size was never the cause of the dark panel.
